messages:
Maya R: quick heads-up from last night's P0 — paging churn + manual followups made the handoff slow. want to propose a lightweight 'watchlist' sync between incident-bot and our post-incident board so action items, customer-impact flags, and handoff notes auto-propagate. thinking minimal MVP: 1) incident-bot emits watchlist entries when customer-impact=true 2) watchlist webhook -> postmortem board creates a card with auto-fields 3) dashboard shows outstanding watchlist items by owner/team
Vikram S: love the idea. can you define what goes into a watchlist entry? is this just actions or also timeline snippets, severity, customer id, affected endpoints?
Maya R: good q. MVP fields: incident_id, severity, affected_customers (list of org ids), brief_impact_line (1 sentence), suggested_owner (team), required_followup (yes/no), proposed_due (ISO date). extra fields later: timeline excerpts, logs, example requests.
Ashley L: also include a postmortem-template-id link so the board can pre-populate the PM draft. that'd cut down on manual copy/paste. we should standardize the template fields to avoid back-and-forth during the review. :+1:
Sam (oncall): paging pain here — sometimes handoff notes are in replies and don't get into the doc. if the bot can capture the last 3 messages of the thread and stash them as 'handoff_notes' that would be huge. also prefer a tag for 'customer-facing' so support knows to send comms.
Jordan H: implementation thoughts: use incident-bot to POST to a small sync service. sync service transforms and sends to board (we can support Jira, GitHub issues, Linear). webhook payload sketch below:
```
POST /sync/watchlist
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-147",
  "severity": "sev2",
  "affected_customers": ["acme-co", "saturn-llc"],
  "impact_line": "Embeddings API returned 504s for >5% of requests between 02:10-02:27 UTC",
  "handoff_notes": "oncall removed bad config, restarted scaler. see logs /tmp/err-324",
  "suggested_owner": "eng-runtime",
  "customer_facing": true,
  "template_id": "pm-thread-compact-v1"
}
```
Jordan H: sync service can also attach a link back to the slack thread and the incident timeline. we should include a short signature so recipients know it was automated (and who to ping).
ops-bot: Incident summary: INC-2026-147 | service: embeddings | duration: 17m | peak-error-rate: 6.3% | affected-customers: 2 | pages: 5 | current-status: postmortem_pending
Maya R: thanks — ops-bot line is perfect to include in payload as metadata.
Vikram S: question on RBAC: who is allowed to mark "required_followup=false"? sometimes engineering marks followups optional after quick cleanup but PMs still want a review. maybe default to required=true and only PM/product can flip it.
Ashley L: agree. default required=true. add an approval field that product can set: { pm_approval: pending/approved/rejected } and we wire triggers to remind PMs after 48 hours if pending.
Sam (oncall): scheduling: can the bot create a tentative postmortem meeting in calendar if required_followup=true and no owner assigned after 24h? auto-propose a slot with oncall + service-owner + eng-sre. saves time.
Jordan H: doable. sync service can call calendar API to propose 3 slots based on oncall rotation. i'd rather leave the final invite to a human but auto-propose helps.
Maya R: ok actionable plan: 1) Jordan & Vikram to spike sync-service prototype (webhook receiver, transform, send to Linear/Jira) — 2 week spike 2) Ashley to publish compact PM template (pm-thread-compact-v1) — by EOW 3) Sam to add handoff-note extractor rules into incident-bot (last 3 messages + explicit /handoff capture) — 4 days 4) ops-bot to expose a single-line incident summary API for payloads (small change) — 2 days
Jordan H: i'll throw up a repo and ping you when initial endpoint is ready. naming: /sync/watchlist v1.
Vikram S: for tracking, can we surface watchlist items in a 'Followups' dashboard with filters: team, owner, customer, due, pm-status? would like to avoid yet another manual spreadsheet.
Ashley L: yep that's the goal. dashboard should also show sla for customer-facing followups (e.g., must have comms within 72h).
Sam (oncall): quick UX note — when bot auto-creates a card, add a comment in the slack thread like: "remediation-bot: created followup card #LR-342 — assigned to eng-runtime (Jordan H)." so humans can see the record.
remediation-bot: created followup card LR-342 | owner: eng-runtime | due: 2026-03-18 | pm_status: pending | link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/LR-342
Maya R: scheduling PM: propose Thu 18:00 UTC — 30m. can we auto-fill attendees: oncall at time of incident (Sam), service lead (Jordan H), product rep (Ashley L), eng-sre rep (Vikram S), and recording link?
Jordan H: fine with that time. I'll make the sync service emit calendar-proposal payload with 3 options and attendees prefilled.
Ashley L: i'll craft the short PM agenda template: impact summary, timeline + root-cause hypothesis, mitigations, followups (owner/due), comms plan. keep it to 30m for quick incidents.
Maya R: OK final asks: - Jordan & Vikram start spike and open WIP PRs - Ashley posts pm-thread-compact-v1 in #docs-devex - Sam adds handoff capture to incident-bot - ops-bot endpoint change (engineers: please coordinate)
Maya R: i'll follow up with a short kickoff thread and add a tracking label 'followup-sync-priority' to the new repo. thanks all :pray:
